4996ec56 typing: a fn no annotation wraps is typed once, by typed_fn, and read from there
//! `if cond { a } else { b }` — the expression form: both branches
//! present, both typed, one taken. The `if` keyword anchor merges
//! ahead of the spine's NAME branch, like the boolean literals.
//! ELSELESS `if cond { statements }` is the statement form, on one
//! line or many — the guard idiom's home. Elseless keeps the two
//! forms unambiguous; the opening BREAK keeps single-line
//! expression arms out of the statement parse.
use features.{LanguageFeature}
use features.if_expr.{when_ladder}
use @std.grammar.{Grammar, Rule, Alt, Seq, Item, Prim, Rep, Build, Expect, Recover}

export fn if_expr() -> LanguageFeature {
    LanguageFeature if_expr {
        gram: grammar {
            stmt = value:if_stmt END -> Stmt.ExprStmt
            stmt_block = "{" ( stmts:stmt | BREAK )* "}" -> Expr.Block
            if_stmt = "if" cond:expression on_true:stmt_block ( "else" ( on_false:stmt_block | on_false:if_stmt ) )? -> Expr.If @head(cond)
            primary = "if" cond:expression on_true:block "else" ( on_false:block | on_false:if_expr ) @expect("else", "an `if` expression needs its `else` branch") -> Expr.If @head(cond)
            if_expr = "if" cond:expression on_true:block "else" ( on_false:block | on_false:if_expr ) -> Expr.If @head(cond)
        }

```
//! The lowering rule of every `if` whose condition binds nothing: a region on the condition, its
//! block in one arm and its `else` (a block, another `if`, or nothing) in the other. An `if` is a
//! core primitive, never a `match` on a `bool`: only `if x is .V(p)` takes a meaning, the match
//! its binding is spelled by.
use core.{ExprId, Lowering, Lowers, Reg, SignedType, owned_type}
use core.expr.{If}

impl Lowers for If {
    /// A region of the `if`'s type on the condition: the block where it holds, else the `else`, or
    /// nothing where there's none.
    fn lowered(mut cx: Lowering, e: ExprId) -> Reg {
        let ty? = cx.type_at(e) else { return cx.unlowered(e) }
        cx
            .region(cx.lower(self.cond), cx.laid_out(ty)) { cx -> branch(cx, self.on_true, ty) } else { cx -> branch_or_nothing(cx, self.on_false, ty) }
    }

    /// A region on the condition whose arms are run for what they do.
    fn lowered_dropped(mut cx: Lowering, e: ExprId) -> Reg {
        cx
            .void_branches(cx.lower(self.cond)) { cx -> let _ = cx.dropped(self.on_true) } else { cx -> if self.on_false != null { let _ = cx.dropped(self.on_false!) } }
        cx.hollow_of(owned_type("void"))
    }
}

/// A branch's value, or where it leaves, nothing of the `if`'s type `ty`.
fn branch(mut cx: Lowering, x: ExprId, ty: SignedType) -> Reg {
    let made = cx.lower(x)
    if cx.store.leaves(x) { cx.hollow_of(ty) } else { made }
}

/// The `else`'s value, or where there's none or it leaves, nothing of the `if`'s type `ty`.
fn branch_or_nothing(mut cx: Lowering, x: ExprId?, ty: SignedType) -> Reg {
    let v? = x else { return cx.hollow_of(ty) }
    branch(cx, v, ty)
}

// AN ARM THAT YIELDS A VALUE ITS ENCLOSING SCOPE OWNS, dying at the merge, hands that scope's
// reference to the merge: the other arms release it on their own way out. A value read past the
// merge, or owned by a scope further out than the branch's, keeps its count.
type Bag = { items: List<int>, name: string }

fn fresh(n: int) -> Bag { Bag { items: [i for i in 0..n], name: "b${n}" } }

fn maybe(n: int) -> Bag? { if n > 0 { fresh(n) } else { null } }

fn picked(n: int, flag: bool) -> Bag {
    let a = fresh(n)
    let b = if flag { a } else { fresh(n + 1) }
    b
}

fn read_past(n: int, flag: bool) -> int {
    let a = fresh(n)
    let b = if flag { a } else { fresh(n + 1) }
    b.items.length + a.items.length
}

fn looped(n: int) -> int {
    let a = fresh(n)
    mut total = 0
    for i in 0..3 {
        let b = if i == 1 { a } else { fresh(i) }
        total = total + b.items.length
    }
    total
}

fn switched(n: int) -> Bag {
    let a = fresh(n)
    match n % 3 { 0 -> a, 1 -> fresh(10), _ -> a }
}

fn left_early(n: int, flag: bool) -> Bag {
    let a = fresh(n)
    let b = if flag {
        a
    } else {
        if n > 5 { return fresh(0) }
        fresh(n + 1)
    }
    b
}

fn insisted(n: int) -> Bag {
    let v? = maybe(n) else { return fresh(7) }
    v
}

fn kept_twice(n: int, flag: bool) -> List<Bag> {
    let a = fresh(n)
    let b = if flag { a } else { fresh(n + 1) }
    [b, a]
}

let p = picked(2, true)
let q = picked(2, false)
let s0 = switched(3)
let s1 = switched(4)
let s2 = switched(5)
let e0 = left_early(2, true)
let e1 = left_early(9, false)
let e2 = left_early(2, false)
let k = kept_twice(4, true)
"${p.items.length} ${q.items.length} ${read_past(2, true)} ${read_past(2, false)} ${looped(4)} ${s0.name} ${s1.name} ${s2.name} ${e0.name} ${e1.name} ${e2.name} ${insisted(3).name} ${insisted(0).name} ${k[0].name} ${k[1].items.length}"

#!/bin/sh
# THE CENSUS COMPILER: the cli this tree builds, over a runtime compiled with -DAVRA_CENSUS, written
# to <out>. It counts exactly what the shipping compiler does and never ships: the shipping runtime
# library is rebuilt before this answers, and the cli's own product is gone.
#   sh tools/census_compiler.sh build/avra.census
#
# THE BUILDER IS build/avra unless CENSUS_BUILDER names another: a layout rule is the BUILDING
# compiler's, so a census of a rule builds the census compiler with a compiler that has it.
set -eu
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
out=${1:-build/avra.census}
builder=${CENSUS_BUILDER:-build/avra}
[ -x "$builder" ] || { echo "census: no $builder to build the census compiler with — run \`make avra\` first"; exit 1; }
# A MADE BOX IS NAMED BY ITS CALLER'S CALLER, two frames up, which only frame pointers reach:
# macOS keeps them always, Linux only when asked, in the runtime and in every emitted fn.
counted="-DAVRA_CENSUS -fno-omit-frame-pointer"
shipping() {
    make --no-print-directory build/libavra_runtime.a > /dev/null 2>&1 || \
        echo "census: the shipping runtime did NOT rebuild — run \`make build/libavra_runtime.a\`"
    find packages/cli/src/main packages/cli/src/main.av.ll -maxdepth 0 -delete 2> /dev/null || :
}
trap shipping EXIT INT TERM
make --no-print-directory C
…[585 chars cut]…
 build packages/cli > build/census-build.out 2>&1 || {
    tail -20 build/census-build.out; echo "census: the census compiler did not build"; exit 1; }
# A BINARY THE PROGRAM LAYER PLACES IS ITS KEPT BINARY, LINKED: a census compiler left from an earlier
# run can be that same file, which `mv` will not move onto itself — the old one goes first.
[ ! -e "$out" ] || find "$out" -delete
mv packages/cli/src/main "$out"
# A C symbol wears a leading underscore on macOS and none on Linux.
nm "$out" | grep -Eq '[ _]note_retain$' || { echo "census: $out carries no census — refusing to report"; exit 1; }

//! What an `if` means, in the core.
use core.{At}
use features.{TypedCode, meaning, typed_coded}

/// `if c { a } else { b }` is a match on the condition; without an else, the other arm does nothing.
export meaning if_else {
    quote { if ${c} { ${..taken} } else { ${..other} } } -> quote {
        match ${c} {
            true -> {
                ${taken}
            }
            _ -> {
                ${other}
            }
        }
    },
    quote { if ${c} { ${..taken} } } if elseless(it) -> quote {
        match ${c} {
            true -> {
                ${taken}
            }
            _ -> {
                ${nothing_in(it)}
            }
        }
    },
}

/// Whether the `if` has no else.
fn elseless(subject: TypedCode) -> bool {
    match subject.at {
        .Expr(e) -> match subject.of.view.store.expr(e) { .If(_, _, other) -> other == null, rest -> false },
        .Stmt(_) or .Pat(_) or .Field(_, _) or .Param(_, _) -> false,
    }
}

/// No statements, in the item `subject` stands in.
fn nothing_in(subject: TypedCode) -> List<TypedCode> { typed_coded(subject.of, []) }

/// The tag of the variant a pattern asks for, absent for one that binds a payload or names no
/// variant of `variants`.
fn asked_tag(store: SyntaxArena, variants: List<VariantSeat>, p: PatId) -> int? {
    match store.pat(p) {
        .Variant(name, args) -> if args.all((a) -> holed(store, a)) { variants.find_index(it.name == name.of) } else { null },

    }

    match store.pat(p) { .Wild -> true, rest -> false }

--- content ---
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""The cost slice of a head judged against its base's, both run on this machine by tools/cost.sh:
  python3 cost_vs_base.py <tree>/tools <base build/cost dir> <head build/cost dir>
Each row of the base's run is the baseline row, judged by cost_ratchet's own judge (its tolerance),
and the summary line is the one `make cost` prints."""
import os
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, sys.argv[1])
import cost_ratchet as cr  # noqa: E402

base_dir, head_dir = sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3]
snaps = [open(os.path.join(d, "snapshot")).read().strip() for d in (base_dir, head_dir)]
if snaps[0] != snaps[1]:
    print("cost: base measured %s, head %s — not one snapshot" % tuple(snaps))
    sys.exit(1)
base, now = cr.measured(base_dir), cr.measured(head_dir)
if not base or not now:
    print("cost: a run printed no counts — refusing to judge")
    sys.exit(1)
failed, fell = cr.judge(now, base)
for line in fell + failed:
    print(line)
print("cost: %d rows, %d over, %d fell (head vs base, snapshot %s, tolerance %g%%)"
      % (len(base), len(failed), len(fell), snaps[0][:8], cr.TOLERANCE_PPM / 10000))
sys.exit(1 if failed else 0)

//! What a `for` loop means, in the core.
use core.{At, Stmt, SyntaxArena}
use features.{TypedCode, meaning}

/// `for x in xs { … }` over a list walks its positions up to its length, read once — a text's `chars`
/// view, which is no list until one is asked for, is walked by the statement's own rule; `for i in
/// lo..hi { … }` counts from `lo` up to `hi`, each read once. Each turn binds the element or the count, and
/// counts past it before the body runs, so a `continue` never turns forever.
export meaning for_each {
    quote { for ${x} in ${xs} { ${..body} } } if walks_a_list(xs) && !views_chars(xs) && !breaks_by_label(body) -> quote {
        let items = ${xs}
        let count = items.length
        mut at = 0
        while at < count {
            let ${x} = items[at]
            at = at + 1
            ${body}
        }
    },
    quote { for ${i} in ${lo}..${hi} { ${..body} } } if !breaks_by_label(body) -> quote {
        mut at = ${lo}
        let end = ${hi}
        while at < end {
            let ${i} = at
            at = at + 1
            ${body}
        }
    },
}

/// Whether the subject is a list, as typing found it.
fn walks_a_list(xs: TypedCode) -> bool { xs.type()?.listed() != null }

/// Whether the subject is a `chars()` view.
fn views_chars(xs: TypedCode) -> bool {
    match xs.at {
        .Expr(e) -> match xs.of.view.store.expr(e) {
            .MethodCall(_, name, args) -> name.of == "chars" && args.is_empty(),
            rest -> false,
        }

### 2026-11-20T20:15:45 AGENT
<to_controller>`for` design (not built):
1. **What the meaning makes.** `for_each` turns each list or range `for` into a `while`. For a list: `let items = xs; let count = items.length; mut at = 0; while at < count { let x = items[at]; at = at + 1; body }`. For a range: `mut at = lo; let end = hi; while at < end { let i = at; at = at + 1; body }`. That is 28,955 made nodes over 2,290 sites, 12.6 per site.
2. **What the primitive removes: all of it.** `ForEach.stmt_lowered` already lowers every `for` the meaning refuses (index, label, map, octets, chars, source) with the walk verbs: `walk_list`/`walk_range` + `walk_turn` (LoopStart, LoopCond, step before the body, so `continue` can't spin) + `walked_element`, and no tick on the back edge. So the plan deletes `for_each`, and list and range loops take that one rule, as `if` did. `cx.walking` goes with it, since its only job was to keep tick tests off the meaning's `while`.
3. **Readers that need the meaning: none by name.** Only generic fallbacks read it: `check_stmt` falls to ForEach's own `stmt_checked`, lists `kept_types` to its kids, `lower_stmt` to `stmt_lowered`, `item_elaborated` only counts it. Nothing names `for_each`, and idioms/laws/fmt read the surface. I'll grep again for anything matching a `while` shaped like a walk before building.
4. **Watch item.** A written `lo..hi` should go straight to `walk_count(lo, hi)`, not build a Range to take apart.
5. **Receipts as for `if`.** IR golden of a list `for`, a range `for` and a `for` with `continue`, before vs after. A native diff of one hot walk. The cost slice head vs base.
6. **Predicted cold save, measured the same way.** This scales the `if` result (lowering −1.7 to −2.7 s in the bodies wave; build-cli retains −1.50%) by made nodes: 28,955 against 109,145, or 26.5%. That gives lowering −0.45 to −0.7 s, build-cli retains about −0.4%, check rows about −0.02%. Typing stays flat: ForEach's typing of made nodes is 0.21 s, and the If's 1.39 s didn't show up either.
7. **Extra save, not counted above.** Today `items[at]` takes the index read's path; `walked_element` is a plain `element_at`. If the index read carries a bounds check, that check is saved too. The IR golden will show whether it does.
</to_controller>

fn nested_managed(rows: List<List<string>>) -> string {
    mut out = ""

                    if note.length > 0 { break row }
                },

                _ -> { out = out + up + " " },
            }

    }

}

type Bag = { items: List<string> }

fn popped() -> string {
    mut xs = ["a", "b", "c", "d"]
    mut out = ""
    for x in xs {
        let _ = xs.pop()
        out = out + x
    }
    "${out}/${xs.length}"
}

fn rebound() -> string {
    mut xs = ["p", "q", "r"]
    mut out = ""
    for x in xs {
        xs = []
        out = out + x
    }
    "${out}/${xs.length}"
}

fn overwritten() -> string {
    mut xs = ["1", "2", "3"]
    mut out = ""
    for i, x in xs {
        if i + 1 < xs.length { xs.set(i + 1, "z") }
        out = out + x
    }
    "${out}/${xs.join("")}"
}

fn field_emptied() -> string {
    mut b = Bag { items: ["k", "l", "m"] }
    mut out = ""
    for x in b.items {
        b.items = []
        out = out + x
    }
    "${out}/${b.items.length}"
}

fn celled() -> string {
    let c = Cell.new(["u", "v", "w"])
    mut out = ""
    for x in c.get() {
        c.set([])
        out = out + x
    }
    "${out}/${c.get().length}"
}

"${popped()} ${rebound()} ${overwritten()} ${field_emptied()} ${celled()}"
EOF

# Zero cost — the registry

The law (CLAUDE.md, "PERFORMANT BY DEFAULT"): idiomatic code IS the fast code. A writer never
hand-tunes a representation; the compiler chooses it, and the cost of what was written is visible
and gated. This file is the registry the law is held to: one row per technique, each with the
DETECTOR that finds its candidates. A technique without a detector is a wish, not a row.

## Detectors — how candidates are found

Four instruments, each reading what the compiler or the runtime already knows (P10). None is a
human reading code.

| detector | reads | finds | where |
|---|---|---|---|
| **census sites** | the runtime's exact per-site counters (boxes, retains, releases, clones, string compares, list writes) over the fixed workloads | the hottest sites, each CLASSIFIED to the technique that would remove its cost (below) | `avra census --candidates` |
| **missed-optimization remarks** | the compiler at the moment a technique declines to fire | WHY a site paid, as a TYPED reason per technique (`Declined`: `DeferDecline`, `ProbeDecline`, `SettleDecline`, `ConsumeDecline`, `DynDecline`, `PackDecline`), its words rendered by one voice fn | `avra explain --cost @fn`, grouped by reason and counted; `cost_remarks` is a query, so the remarks are facts in the DB. A build never notes them: zero cost unless asked |
| **shape rules** | the source, as `rule` declarations `avra check` finds | the patterns that cost by construction | `avra check`, ratcheted like idioms

never shrinks under it. The place proves the slot, so the guard `avra_array_get` asked of each

rebound, overwritten, its field emptied, its cell emptied, or emptied by a comprehension's element,
is walked as it was. docs/ZERO_COST.md gains the bounds-check elimination row, its detector the
`index_walk` shape rule, whose fix is the walk.

```
# One run of the census compiler in the snapshot, once what it reads is older than the stamp window:
# its census to <name>.out, what it printed to <name>.stdout. The machine's store is off unless the
# workload's `store` is `filled`: then on, in the run's own cache, which every cold run starts bare.
counted() {
    name=$1; shift
    machine=0
    [ "${store:-off}" != filled ] || machine=1
    sleep 3
    started=$(date +%s)
    # the census reports at exit only where the run accounts (AVRA_MEM_STATS)
    (cd "$src" && unset AVRA_MACHINE_STORE_DIR && AVRA_MACHINE_STORE=$machine AVRA_MEM_STATS=1 AVRA_WORK_AHEAD_OFF=1 AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0 AVRA_CACHE_DIR="$cache" AVRA_STORE_KEPT_HERE=1 \
        sh "$root/tools/memcap.sh" "${COST_CAP_MB:-8000}" taskset -c 0 build/avra "$@" \
        > "$root/$out/$name.stdout" 2> "$root/$out/$name.out") || {
        tail -20 "$out/$name.out"; echo "cost: $name failed ($*)"; exit 1; }
    echo "cost: $name $(($(date +%s) - started)) s"
}

# One warm findings run of the cli, its `worked:` line kept as <name>.out, its census beside it.
warm() {
    counted "$1" tapes --findings packages/cli
    mv "$out/$1.out" "$out/$1.census"
    grep '^worked: ' "$out/$1.census" > "$out/$1.out" || { echo "cost: $1 printed no worked line"; exit 1; }
}

    cat << 'EOF'
check-cli off check --counts packages/cli
build-cli off build packages/cli
check-program off check --counts packages/std-program
cold-with-store-fill filled check --counts packages/cli
EOF
}

Guarded reads measured, not built. The probe was a census-only caller table on the three guarded read rows: `avra_array_get`, `avra_array_get_owned`, `avra_slot_present`.
- It ran in a census compiler (a release build of the cli) built by walk-bounds' own gen-2, over the cost snapshot a6d0d0a0, cold, store off, on one core.

- Detector 1, `index_walk`: 0 sites in the idioms baseline. No counted loop indexes its own list anywhere, so the census supplies the rest.

Top-60 guarded sites: 1.96 G (check) and 2.43 G (build). I ranked them by class, sorting each site by its call (constant vs dynamic index, the callee, the Avra fn).

**1. Box slots the box's type proves: 837 M (42.7%) check, 1,142 M (47.0%) build.**
- Sites: enum tag reads (`tag_of`, slot 0) and payload reads (`payload_at`, slot 1+k), a fn box's code (`code_of`, slot 0), a task's answer cell (`awaited_reg`, slot 0), and the nullable slot-box unwrap.
- Examples: `SavedSource.word_at`'s `match` alone is 221 M across three sites, at slots 0 and 1. `hash_of_answer_held`'s cells come to 86 M. `token_mask` calls through `lex.wears_kind`.
- Today all of these go through the guarded `slot_read`, while declared record fields already use `proven_read` (`avra_slot_get`).
- Proof needed: the type's shape, the same rule `proven_read` uses. For a payload, the tag test in front of the read, i.e. the match arm or `is` test, has already chosen the variant. This is the biggest class and the cheapest fix: one verb swap per call site in core/boxed.av and the closure and task verbs.

**2. Masked hash probes: 391 M (19.9%) check, 416 M (17.1%) build.**
- Sites: `HashKeyedTable.position_at`, `free_slot`, `ReadTable.row_at`, `IndexTable.position_of`.
- Provable: `slots[h & (slots.length - 1)]`, where `0 ≤ h & (n-1) < n` once `n > 0` holds before it (`if slots.is_empty() { return }`). A one-node value-range rule on `&` whose mask is the list's own length minus one, over a list unchanged between the length read and the index. The snapshot argument from walk-bounds covers the "unchanged" part.
- Not provable locally: `highs[position]` and `lows[position]`. `position` comes out of the table, so those reads need the table's invariant and stay guarded. Expect roughly half of this class's count to go.

**3. Reads by a counter that a comparison bounds: 223 M (11.3%) check, 239 M (9.8%) build.**
- Sites: the sorted merges (`merge_word_runs`, `WordColumns.before`).
- Provable: `order[first]` under `first < middle` where `middle = smaller_of(…, order.length)`. That needs a relational proof: a dominating `i < m` with `m ≤ xs.length` and no write in between.
- Not provable without an invariant: `highs[a]` with `a` taken out of `order`, a permutation.
- This is the hardest of the three, so it ranks below 2 even though its count is close.

**Not ranked:**
- Other dynamic (17–21%) is heterogeneous: `cannot_take`'s three parallel per-token columns (97 M), `token_wears_kind` into a static table by kind id (83 M), and `RootIndex.picked` (48 M). Each needs an invariant across lists, so none has a local proof.
- The evaluator's register reads (`Machine.run_body`/`step`/`at`, 5%) are bounded by the IR's register count.
- Arena reads by a minted id (`SyntaxArena.expr`, 1–3% once its constant tag reads are counted in class 1) would need the grow-only-id proof from the parked lent/Grown work.

**Recommendation:** take 1 next. It is about 45% of the top guarded reads, needs no new analysis, and swaps rows in the verbs that already have the proof. Then 2, as a range rule on `&`.

// proves: a payload read with no bounds test only where a test of its enum's tag that chose its
// variant stands before it, and every other way to a payload still answers rightly — a switch's
// case and its arm for the rest, a chain's tested arms and its untested last, nested variants, an
// or-pattern, a guard, a catch naming some or all of an error's variants, `?`, `is`, a task's cell
// and a fn box's code, each over variants of different widths in one enum.
enum Shape {
    Dot
    Line(len: int)
    Rect(w: int, h: int)
    Named(label: string, inner: Shape)
}

enum Fault {
    Short(n: int)
    Long(text: string)
}

fn area(s: Shape) -> int {
    match s {
        .Dot -> 0
        .Line(len) -> len
        .Rect(w, h) -> w * h
        .Named(_, inner) -> area(inner)
    }
}

fn nested(s: Shape) -> string {
    match s {
        .Named(label, .Rect(w, _)) -> "${label}:${w}"
        .Named(label, .Line(len)) -> "${label}-${len}"
        .Line(n) or .Rect(n, _) -> "n${n}"
        _ -> "?"
    }
}

fn guarded(s: Shape) -> int {
    match s {
        .Rect(w, h) if w > h -> w
        .Rect(_, h) -> h
        .Line(len) if len > 2 -> len * 10
        _ -> 1
    }
}

fn faulty(k: int) -> Result<int, Fault> {
    if k == 0 { return .Ok(7) }
    if k == 1 { return .Err(Fault.Short(k)) }
    .Err(Fault.Long("long${k}"))
}

fn caught_all(k: int) -> string {
    let r = faulty(k) catch {
        .Short(n) -> n * 100
        .Long(text) -> text.length
    }
    "${r}"
}

fn caught_some(k: int) -> Result<int, Fault> {
    let r = faulty(k) catch { .Short(n) -> n + 40 }
    .Ok(r + 1)
}

fn asked(k: int) -> Result<int, Fault> {
    let v = faulty(k)?

/// The position of a unit marker (`LoopStart`, `LoopEnd`).
fn marker_index(ins: List<Ins>, marker: Ins) -> int {
    // LICENSED loops.push_loop: an index scan — the position is the answer
    for j, i in ins {
        if same_marker(i, marker) { return j }
    }
    0 - 1
}

fn same_marker(i: Ins, marker: Ins) -> bool {
    i is .LoopStart && marker is .LoopStart || i is .LoopEnd && marker is .LoopEnd
}

/// A fn's IR by name, from the rendered module.
/// How many times `word` stands in `text`.
fn times(text: string, word: string) -> int { text.split(word).length - 1 }

    let rest = text.substring(at, text.length)

    if end < 0 { rest } else { rest.substring(0, end) }
}

boxes: a slot the box's type proves is read with no bounds test

An enum box lays its tag first, a fn box its code, a joined task its one cell: each read is of a
slot the box's type proves is there, and now reads through `proven_read` (`avra_slot_get`), as a
declared record field already did. A payload is proven only past a test of its enum's tag that
chose its variant, standing before the read on every way to it: `payload_proven` reads it there,
and `payload_at` keeps its guard everywhere else.

Where the test stands is the match's to say. `Chosen` carries `tested`: set for an arm entered
through its own accept test (a chain's tested arms, a tail's arms, a switch's cases, an
or-pattern's branch that took), so its whole pattern's tags were chosen; unset for a match's one
arm, a chain's last and a switch's arm for the rest, which no test of their own chose, and for
what an accept test or a guard reads. `?` and a catch read `Ok` past `tag == 0` and the failure
past its negation; a catch's variant and member arms read proven where the switch on the
failure's tag took their case, guarded in its arm for the rest. A failure carried on
(`propagated`) and a union member's payload stay guarded.

payload_proven proves every way to a payload answers rightly over variants of different widths:
a switch's case and its rest, a chain's tested and untested arms, nested variants, an or-pattern,
a guard, a catch naming some or all variants, `?`, `is`, a task's cell and a fn box's code.
lower_test pins a switch's tested case reading proven and its rest guarded.

### 2026-11-21T02:21:56 AGENT
Candidate 2 in IR is a `slot` cell. Every store to it is `x & (avra_array_len(L) - 1)` over the same list register `L`, and the reads are `avra_array_get(L, load cell)`. The emptiness proof is an earlier top-level region on `is_empty(L)` whose taken arm returns. That is a small IR pass, not a verb swap, so I'm posting its design while the receipts for 1 run:

<to_controller>
**Design for candidate 2, the `&`-mask range rule.** Build starts after 1's receipts; nothing else is building.

**The shape it proves.** In IR (rendered from a copy of `position_at`), the probe index is a `mut` cell `c`. Every store to `c` is `x & (n - 1)`, where `n = avra_array_len(L)` over one list register `L`. Every read is `avra_array_get(L, load c)`.
- Proof: `0 ≤ x & (n-1) ≤ n-1 < n` whenever `n ≥ 1`. `L` is a register, so its list never changes length under the fn: a write through any holder copies first, as with walk-bounds.
- The `n ≥ 1` half needs a test of emptiness in front of the reads: a top-level region on `is_empty(L)` (or `L.length == 0`) whose taken arm returns, before the first store to `c`.

**What it is.** A pass over the lowered body: find the masked cells, check every store, check that emptiness test, and rewrite only those reads to `avra_slot_get`. Anything that doesn't match keeps its guard.
- `free_slot` tests no emptiness, so it stays guarded. Its caller `slots_holding` always gives it a non-empty list, but that proof isn't local.
- `highs[row]` and `lows[row]` (the row taken from the table) stay guarded.

**Expected gain.** Of the class's 391–416 M guarded reads, the `slots[slot]` reads in `position_at`, `row_at` and `interned` qualify, roughly half. Each loses a load of `len`, a compare and a branch. Small next to 1: about 0.2 s of a cold build at about 1 ns a read. Receipts as for 1.

If you'd rather not add a pass for this size of win, I'll stop after 1.
</to_controller>
